takeaways: Global growth faces headwinds from energy-driven inflation and geopolitical instability, prompting central banks to diversify into gold as a hedge against dollar-denominated debt and sanctions.
Big Tech faces a valuation reckoning as investors pivot from AI optimism to demanding concrete revenue proof, while rising infrastructure costs force firms to fund their own utility upgrades.
Fixed income markets remain volatile as the U.S. coordinates with Japan to stabilize the yen, while bond traders demand higher duration premiums amid concerns over long-term inflation credibility.

items.title: Global Economy, Hit by Iran War and Inflation, Faces Sharp Slowdown
bullets: The IMF has downgraded its 2026 global output growth projection to 3%, down from 3.5% last year, citing energy supply chain disruptions caused by the conflict with Iran.
Global inflation is expected to accelerate to 4.7% in 2026, driven by elevated commodity prices and the U.S. decision to rescind waivers on Iranian oil sanctions.
items.reason: Significant downward revision to global growth forecasts and rising inflation risks.

items.title: Why Gold Is Emerging as the Reserve Asset of a Multipolar Global Economy
bullets: Central banks are increasingly diversifying reserves into gold to mitigate the risks of dollar-denominated debt and geopolitical sanctions in a multipolar system.
The paradox of a strong U.S. dollar is accelerating this shift, as higher debt-servicing costs and market volatility incentivize reserve managers to seek neutral, non-sovereign assets.
items.reason: Structural shift in global reserve management impacting long-term asset allocation.

items.title: RBI likely to hold rates steady this week as inflation stays manageable despite oil shock
bullets: The Reserve Bank of India is expected to maintain current interest rates, diverging from global peers who are pivoting toward hikes to combat persistent inflation.
Despite the external pressure of an oil price shock, domestic inflation remains within manageable levels, allowing the central bank to prioritize growth stability over immediate tightening.
items.reason: Divergent monetary policy in a major emerging market amid global tightening cycles.

items.title: SpaceX's first-ever earnings report comes as stock hits new all-time low: Q2 preview
bullets: SpaceX is set to release its inaugural earnings report following a June 12 IPO, with the stock currently trading significantly below its $135 offering price at approximately $108.
Investors are closely monitoring the upcoming expiration of insider lockup periods, which could create substantial selling pressure and act as a price ceiling for the stock in the near term.
items.reason: High-profile IPO earnings debut with significant technical pressure from lockup expirations.

items.title: Jobs report and earnings: What NYSE insider Jay Woods is watching this week
bullets: Market participants are bracing for seasonal volatility as August and September historically represent the two worst-performing months for the S&P 500, with average declines of 0.5% and 0.75% respectively since 1990.

Friday's nonfarm payrolls report is a critical focal point, with analysts seeking a 'Goldilocks' unemployment rate of 4.3% to maintain stability in interest rate expectations and avoid triggering further market downside.
items.reason: Macro-economic data and seasonal trends are key drivers for broader market direction.

items.title: US backs yen intervention as fears grow over Japan selling Treasuries
bullets: The US joined Japan in a rare coordinated currency intervention to stabilize the yen, aiming to prevent Tokyo from being forced to liquidate significant holdings of US Treasury securities to fund unilateral support.

To mitigate future risks to the Treasury market, Japan plans to utilize the Federal Reserve’s FIMA Repo Facility, which allows foreign central banks to access dollar liquidity using Treasuries as collateral rather than selling them outright.
items.reason: Systemic risk to the US Treasury market from major foreign holder liquidation.

items.title: Markets Brief: Why Bonds Did the Twist and the Mag 7 Did a Split
bullets: Following Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s press conference, the market experienced a 'twist steepener' where short-term yields fell on dovish signals, while 30-year yields surged to 2007 highs due to concerns over inflation credibility.

Analysts note that Warsh’s remarks suggested the Fed may rely on alternative inflation indicators and market-driven tightening, creating uncertainty that has prompted bond traders to demand higher compensation for long-term duration risk.
items.reason: Shift in Fed communication strategy impacting long-term yield curve dynamics.

items.title: How likely is Beijing to walk the talk on boosting consumption?
bullets: China's second-quarter GDP growth slowed to 4.3% from 5% in the first quarter, highlighting a significant deceleration that brings first-half growth to 4.7%.
Domestic demand is faltering, evidenced by a 5.7% decline in fixed-asset investment and an 18% plunge in property investment, while retail sales growth decelerated sharply to 0.2%.
items.reason: Signals structural weakness in core growth pillars.

items.title: More patient policy framework for China's economy
bullets: The economy is shifting toward an era of 'around 4 percent growth' as it transitions away from traditional real estate and infrastructure engines toward AI and advanced manufacturing.

Economic performance follows a recurring U-shaped rhythm, indicating that while policy support is consistently applied, the economy lacks self-sustaining momentum and remains highly dependent on state intervention.
items.reason: Provides critical context on long-term growth trajectory.

items.title: Hong Kong GDP Growth To Moderate In 2025, UOB Says
bullets: UOB projects a moderation in Hong Kong's GDP growth for 2025, signaling that the economy will fail to replicate the post-pandemic rebound observed in 2024.
Key headwinds include persistent high interest rates, global trade tensions, and a sluggish recovery in mainland China, which continue to dampen both external demand and domestic consumer spending.
items.reason: Macroeconomic outlook shift

items.title: Wheelock Properties' Park Silicon receives almost 7,000 inquiries with prices to be announced soon
bullets: Wheelock Properties' Park Silicon project has generated nearly 7,000 inquiries, with 40% of interest originating from mainland Chinese buyers or frequent cross-border travelers.

The project is positioning itself as a tech-forward development by integrating smart living services and future-proofing for drone delivery, reflecting a strategic shift in developer offerings to attract premium demand.
items.reason: Real estate market sentiment indicator

items.title: Big Tech Earnings Are Sending Valuations in Opposite Directions
bullets: Market divergence has intensified as investors pivot from broad AI optimism to demanding concrete revenue proof, evidenced by Microsoft's record $450 billion market cap gain versus Apple's 7.4% decline on weak iPhone growth forecasts.

Meta's 8% stock drop highlights growing investor sensitivity to capital expenditure, specifically regarding the company's warning that free cash flow could turn negative due to aggressive AI infrastructure spending.
items.reason: Earnings divergence signals a critical shift in how the market values AI-related capital expenditures.

items.title: Big tech to pay more if no deal reached with Australian media
items.source: ABC News & Headlines – Australian Broadcasting Corporation
bullets: The Australian government has increased the potential levy on major digital platforms to 2.5% of local advertising revenue if they fail to secure commercial news-sharing agreements with at least six local publishers.

While the levy rate increased, tech firms secured a significant concession by limiting the tax base to digital advertising revenue rather than total local revenue, potentially reducing the overall financial impact of the regulation.
items.reason: Regulatory changes in Australia set a precedent for global tech taxation and content-sharing obligations.

items.title: EU Artificial Intelligence Act transparency rules now in place across Europe
bullets: The European Commission’s AI Act transparency requirements officially entered into force on August 2, 2026, marking a significant shift in the regulatory landscape for AI developers and deployers.

Companies operating within the EU, including those managing chatbots and AI-generated content, must now comply with mandatory disclosure rules that require users to be explicitly informed when they are interacting with artificial intelligence.
items.reason: Major regulatory milestone impacting global AI compliance costs.

items.title: US scrutinizing Anthropic's artificial intelligence training methods
bullets: The U.S. government has initiated a formal review of Anthropic’s AI training methodologies, signaling increased federal oversight into the data practices of leading foundation model developers.

This scrutiny could set a critical precedent for how AI companies source and utilize training data, potentially impacting the development timelines and operational strategies of major industry players.
items.reason: Direct regulatory risk to a major foundation model provider.

items.title: AMD unveils AI GPU to challenge Nvidia’s Rubin
bullets: AMD's new Instinct MI455X accelerator features 320 billion transistors and 432GB of HBM4 memory, directly challenging Nvidia's Rubin architecture with 50% more memory capacity and higher bandwidth at 23.3 TB/s.

The launch of the Helios rack-scale platform, which integrates 72 GPUs with EPYC processors and Pensando networking, signals AMD's strategic pivot toward selling unified, high-performance AI systems rather than standalone components.
items.reason: Direct competitive threat to Nvidia's flagship product roadmap.

items.title: NVIDIA Stock Forecast Today: NVDA Holds $200 as $250B AI Financing Risk Tests Bulls
bullets: Investors are increasingly concerned that Nvidia may need to provide significant vendor financing or capital guarantees to sustain demand, as evidenced by reports of a potential $250 billion backstop for an OpenAI-linked project.

While Nvidia reported record quarterly revenue of $81.6 billion with 92% of sales coming from data centers, the market is shifting focus toward the sustainability of customer-side infrastructure spending and potential circular-funding risks.
items.reason: Highlights critical concerns regarding AI infrastructure financing sustainability.

items.title: Top Selling Electric Vehicles in the World — June 2026
bullets: Global battery electric vehicle (BEV) registrations grew 21% year-over-year in June, marking the strongest growth rate since September and signaling a rebound for pure electrics despite a 14% decline in plug-in hybrid (PHEV) sales.

Excluding the Chinese and U.S. markets, global EV sales surged 52% year-over-year in June, with BEVs specifically jumping 62%, highlighting significant adoption momentum in emerging and secondary markets.
items.reason: Provides critical global market data and diverging trends between BEVs and PHEVs.

items.title: EVs and hybrids approach half of Australian new car sales amid ongoing fuel crisis
bullets: Australian consumer behavior shifted dramatically in Q2 2026, with electric and hybrid vehicles capturing nearly 50% of new car sales as fuel price volatility drove motorists away from traditional internal combustion engines.

Battery electric vehicle sales more than doubled quarter-over-quarter to 69,414 units, while internal combustion engine market share dropped to a record low of 50.84%, demonstrating the impact of energy security concerns on automotive demand.
items.reason: Illustrates a major regional market shift driven by macroeconomic energy factors.

items.title: Meta, Google Deals Aim to Protect Households From Data Center Power Costs
bullets: Utilities are increasingly mandating that tech giants like Meta and Google directly fund the infrastructure upgrades required for their AI data centers to prevent cost-shifting to residential ratepayers.
A recent agreement between Entergy Louisiana and Meta is projected to generate $2 billion in customer savings over 20 years, signaling a shift toward developer-funded utility expansion models.
items.reason: Highlights a critical regulatory shift in how AI infrastructure costs are allocated.

items.title: Empromptu AI Launches Grid Guard to Stop AI Data Centers From Breaking Their Own Power Infrastructure
bullets: Empromptu AI's new 'Grid Guard' software reduces power volatility in data centers by 80% by staggering GPU workloads, potentially lowering the massive capital expenditures required for redundant power infrastructure.

By smoothing millisecond-level power spikes, this technology addresses a major operational bottleneck for AI training clusters, allowing operators to optimize existing grid capacity rather than overbuilding hardware.
items.reason: Introduces a software-based solution to a major capital-intensive problem in AI infrastructure.

items.title: NASA to hold briefings for upcoming Crew-13 mission to ISS
bullets: The Crew-13 mission, scheduled for mid-September, will transport four astronauts to the International Space Station aboard a SpaceX Dragon spacecraft launched by a Falcon 9 rocket.
Commander Jessica Watkins will make history as the first NASA astronaut to launch on a SpaceX Dragon vehicle twice, leading a crew that includes three first-time space travelers.
items.reason: Highlights continued operational cadence and milestones for NASA-SpaceX commercial crew partnerships.

items.title: FAA proposal eyes fewer regulations for rocket launches, sparking concerns
bullets: The FAA is considering a regulatory framework that would reduce oversight for commercial rocket launches, a move intended to accelerate the industry's rapid expansion.
The proposal has triggered debate regarding the balance between fostering commercial space innovation and maintaining necessary safety standards as launch frequency continues to hit record levels.
items.reason: Regulatory changes directly impact the operational costs and risk profiles of all major commercial space companies.
